item.title: Being Alone:
item.content:encoded: The thing is, though, he got “damn near everything” he wanted at the Foundation, because he was, y’know, a Gary Stu. If you’re working on another interpretation of Duke where he used to a dramatic but not necessarily despicable individual before the Foundation confined him, that’d be neat to see, provided that you intend to show us the cause of the transformation.

item.title: SCP-5870: Re: -1
item.content:encoded:
I now fully understand your points, and I will keep in mind, particularly the fact that I need to improve the tone of my writing style. I apologize if I sounded rude a little, but at several points, I was just confused by some of what you have said.

Hopefully, I rectify in future articles the writing issues you pointed out, because now that I think about it, professional tone is a problem for me. I will also try to make the anomalous part clearer :)

item.title: SCP-5238:
item.content:encoded:
I've been bright, I've been faded
I'm nearly halfway through
Barely believe we made it
When I met eyes with you
I caught a walking fever
I know how all this ends
Palm over my receiver
Cradling me again

-Fleet Foxes, Cradling Mother, Cradling Woman

This piece is dedicated to all those siblings we lost in 2020 to the global machine of transphobia. You deserved better.

And also to PR, for persisting despite the flames.

Thanks to those who helped during the critting process, including cybersqyd, PeppersGhost, PlaguePJP, WarFang, OCuin, and others.

Happy New Year.

item.title: SCP-[even number]-J:
item.content:encoded:
+ Boi
- Ok

Item #: SCP-69-J

Object Class: thaumiel

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-69-J is to be kept in a Butter Chicken-lined containment chamber located in Fort Knox, where it is to be guarded at all times by no less than 3 lawyers armed with Babies .

In the event that SCP-69-J ever begins running its brain, Dr Charles Gears is to fly SCP-69-J until it ceases its behavior. In the event of a containment breach, Mobile Task Force Alpha-7 (''The Office'') is to be dispatched to SCP-69-J's last known location.

Description: SCP-69-J is a THICC Elephant. Like most members of its species, it is able to sell penis, and regularly eats twice its own weight in Butter Chicken each day.

SCP-69-J's unusual properties manifest whenever it comes in contact with Sex, which causes it to turn into man. Whenever this happens, all bars within a 42 kilometer radius will begin to suck uncontrollably, usually leading to civilian casualties.

In addition, many researchers feel it has an uncanny resemblance to Jennifer Lawrence. Whether or not this is at all related to SCP-69-J's anomalous properties is unknown at this time.

Recovery Log: SCP-69-J was first located in McDonaldsville where the Buffallo Bills were using it in order to Melt Mount Fuji Thankfully, Mobile Task Force Alpha-7 (''The Office'') was able to recover the object with only 408157610958016754061789 civilian casualties.

Addendum: Test Log 69-1

Dr. Steinmann: Ello? Ello? Is zhis thing on? Ach, good. Zhis is Docktorr Steinmann, and I am about to test SCP-69's reaction to Touching. Are you ready to proceed, Docktorr Mccoy?
Dr. Mccoy: Yes sir, ready to begin test.

Dr. Steinmann: Excellent! I am now introducing the Touching to 69… hmm, zhe subject seems to have already figured out zhe test material.

Dr. Mccoy: Making a note; 'subject shows high capacity for learning'.

Steinmann: Now zhe subject is lookink right at me, almost as if it… MEIN GOTT! MEIN Liver! IT'S GOT MEIN Liver! OH ZHE AGONY! ZHE AGONEEEEEEEEEEEEY!

END LOG

In light of incident 69-J-1, testing has been suspended indefinitely. - O5-█

item.title: A Second Chance:
item.content:encoded:
I appreciate the feedback and I hope the next thing I write down is not as horribly put together as this one.

You can always revise the material and repost it once it's been edited significantly. I recommend that you follow the feedback-seeking process noted in the How to Write an SCP Guide (it's pretty much exactly the same process for tales).

item.title: A Second Chance:
item.content:encoded: To answer your question, no. Yes you’re right. I totally should have. I understood from the beginning that it would not turn out well, but I posted it anyway like an idiot. You’re right about the dialogue. Reading it aloud it sounds like these two characters aren’t people. The Capitalisation errors however I was completely unaware of. I think I sometimes press shift on accident when I type too fast. The repetitive dialogue is a result of my inability to “think on my feet” while writing and change up the way I phrase things. The period in the title was another habit. I’ll fix it soon. I appreciate the feedback and I hope the next thing I write down is not as horribly put together as this one.

item.title: A Second Chance:
item.content:encoded:
Author, out of curiosity, did you happen to get the material critiqued before posting? There are a lot of simple errors, from inconsistent paragraph spacing to overly repetitive dialogue tags (also, the capitalization in the title is inconsistent, and the period seems unnecessary).

The dialogue itself also feels quite wooden; when read out loud, the speech doesn't really sound like real people speaking. Also, the verb tense changes.

Sorry, but I am downvoting this because I feel like it needs substantially more work before I would feel confident giving an upvote.
